clue.text: Returning to unload the scenery

parts.note: coming back, so returning gives the word back
to drop goods is to unload them

explanation.surface: Stagehands coming back to strip the set after a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage is part of a theatre's set.

clue.text: Wedding path, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound but different spelling

parts.note: a bridle path is a track for horse riders, so bridle can stand for the path

explanation.surface: The aisle walked at a wedding, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: A bridle path (or bridleway) is a British track for riders; 'say' turns BRIDLE into its sound-alike BRIDAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives: anything belonging to a marriage ceremony or a bride is described this way.

clue.text: Accountant's lady, one having gloomy views

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant; the possessive adds S
Sandra is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper's wife who always expects the worst.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Trojan prophetess was fated to foretell disaster and never be believed, so her name is used for any prophet of doom.
explanation.definitionFit: The name now means a pessimist whose warnings of doom go unheeded.

clue.text: Failure gone wrong causes resentment

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: gone wrong means the letters of gone are set awry and rearranged

explanation.surface: A flop that goes badly breeds ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in high dudgeon is to feel deep indignation or offence.

clue.text: Love to have a range of knowledge about a tree

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
ken means one's scope of understanding, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Someone who loves knowing all about one particular tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means made of or relating to the oak, a familiar hardwood.

clue.text: Energetic performance I have concluded

indicators.note: concluded tells us the contracted I have comes at the close, after the first piece

parts.note: an act is a turn or performance on stage
I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: A lively show that the performer has just finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lively and busy is the same as being full of energy.

clue.text: School pudding?

explanation.surface: A dessert served at a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A place of higher learning, and also a traditional steamed suet pudding with dried fruit, the college pudding.

clue.text: Five-sevenths of state making up the country

indicators.note: keeping five of the seven letters of the state name means the last two are dropped

parts.note: Indiana is a US state

explanation.surface: Most of a state forming a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A large nation of South Asia.

clue.text: Choosing to be at cross-purposes in middle age

parts.note: elect, as in president-elect, means chosen but not yet in office, so soon to be
taken as written

indicators.note: middle picks out the central letter of the word age

explanation.surface: Picking the wrong goals once one reaches midlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at cross-purposes' adds a hint at the definition: voters choose by marking a cross on the ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Electing is choosing someone by vote, typically with a cross on a ballot.

clue.text: Mild way to reprove

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
to rate is an old verb meaning to scold or reprove

explanation.surface: A gentle method of telling someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something temperate, not extreme, is gentle or mild.

clue.text: Comprehensive information a surgeon needs?

parts.note: the phrase for privileged, insider facts is read literally as knowing what lies within the body, which a surgeon must

explanation.surface: Thorough data a surgeon requires.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means confidential facts known to insiders, here also anatomy within the body.

clue.text: A menial was lost on the north coast of Egypt

definitions.text: on the north coast of Egypt

indicators.note: was lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be reassembled

explanation.surface: A servant went astray along Egypt's northern shore.
explanation.walkthrough: El Alamein is the Egyptian coastal town where decisive Second World War battles were fought in 1942.
explanation.definitionFit: The town lies on the Mediterranean shore west of Alexandria.

clue.text: Graceful gent, ale bespattered

indicators.note: bespattered means splashed about, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dapper man gets beer splashed all over him.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and refined in manner or appearance.

clue.text: Antedate other toothless animals

indicators.note: other asks for a different arrangement of the letters of the word before

explanation.surface: Predating some other creatures without teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The scientific order name for mammals such as sloths, anteaters and armadillos, which lack front teeth.

clue.text: Unqualified sailor therefore has musical instrument

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
so means therefore
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A sailor without training who happens to play an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and without reservation, as in an absolute ban.

clue.text: Man in bed wincing

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man lying in bed flinching with pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, used as an example of a man.

clue.text: Flew round in a flap, that's marvellous!

indicators.note: in a flap means agitated, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A bird flapped around excitedly: amazing!
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean wonderfully good or amazing.

clue.text: Lily lops head off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are out of order and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone decapitates a lily.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a member of the lily family, the flower of the Elysian fields in Greek myth.

clue.text: Incline to give a point of view

explanation.surface: Leaning one way to offer an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope or tilt, and also a particular bias or angle on a story.

clue.text: Part-exchange business fashionable

parts.note: trade is commerce or business
in means fashionable, as in the in thing

explanation.surface: A stylish firm offering part-exchange deals.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing over an old item as partial payment for a new one.

clue.text: George, the blind pianist, gives the woman a ring

parts.note: she refers to a woman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous musician presents a lady with jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: George Shearing was a blind British-born jazz pianist, composer of Lullaby of Birdland.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the jazz musician George, born blind in London in 1919.

clue.text: Repair retail outlet again first

indicators.note: first places the word for again at the front, before the shop

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Reopening a mended shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring back to good condition is to mend or fix.

clue.text: Rode round Dartmouth

parts.note: a cycle is a round, a complete series
the mouth of the Dart is its first letter, D

explanation.surface: Someone biked around a Devon town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmouth is a Devon port; read as 'Dart mouth' it gives the opening letter of Dart.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride a bicycle is to have pedalled along, a kind of riding.

clue.text: Nothing left out of this container?

definitions.text: Nothing left out of this container?

parts.words: Nothing left out of this container?
parts.note: a bag that keeps everything inside, with nothing omitted, describes a big travelling case

explanation.surface: Is nothing missing from this box?
explanation.definitionFit: A large bag for carrying all of a traveller's possessions.

clue.text: Beam when Sarah turns up with cockney lady

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means the short name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Sal is a short form of Sarah
a cockney drops the h of her

explanation.surface: A girl appears beside a London woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow concentrated ray of light.

clue.text: It's a puzzle when first person's tyres exploded

parts.note: my is the first-person possessive

indicators.note: exploded means blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling case of one's own tyres bursting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something baffling or unexplained, an enigma.

clue.text: Fellow gently entering plant

indicators.note: entering puts the soft sign inside the word for fellow

parts.note: a fellow is a male
p, piano, is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: A man quietly going into a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree, the sycamore family, so a plant.

clue.text: As much as can be eaten in one go during the final course of a meal?

definitions.text: As much as can be eaten in one go during the final course of a meal?

parts.words: As much as can be eaten in one go during the final course of a meal?
parts.note: a single mouthful of pudding is the measure a particular spoon holds

explanation.surface: How much pudding one bite holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A measure of quantity equal to what one spoon of the sweet-course size holds.

clue.text: Lines not initially included in loose part of pipe

indicators.note: included in puts these letters within the word for loose

parts.note: lax means slack or loose
RY, railway, gives lines

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of not

explanation.surface: Part of a pipe has come loose, with lines left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' reads as 'not at first' but just gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: The voice box sits at the top of the windpipe.

clue.text: Discovered some meat in the grass

indicators.note: in puts the meat inside the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
veal is meat from a calf

explanation.surface: Found some beef lying in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Made known or uncovered, so found out.
